newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. warns of mass hunger in ex-Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. warns of mass hunger in ex-Yugoslavia.

text.p: More than two million people risk going hungry in former Yugoslavia this spring unless the international community provides more food aid, the United Nations food agency said on Thursday.
The World Food Programme (WFP) said in a statement it feared social stability in Bosnia could be undermined if some 1.8 million needy people there do not receive basic food rations.
Shortage of food would also affect hundreds of thousands of refugees in Serbia, Montenegro and eastern Slavonia.
It said wheat flour supplies would run out in March in the Yugoslav Federal Republic, in April in eastern Slavonia and in May in Bosnia.
Some 2.2 million people would risk being left without their staple ration of bread, the WFP said.
It called for immediate donations because pledged food takes three months to reach beneficiaries.
The statement said WFP officials feared the peace process in former Yugoslavia and the lifting of sanctions had led many to forget the humanitarian plight of millions of people in the area.
